Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you when high blood pressure may be present, but they do not provide actual blood pressure readings.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but they require periodic calibration with a traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to offer full blood pressure measurement without any calibration, citing clinical trial results involving thousands of participants……

The Silent Killer

Both abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) pose serious health threats.

Of the two, hypertension is more dangerous and is even known as the "silent killer" — it can cause serious and irreversible damage to the arteries, heart and brain, yet shows no obvious symptoms. Many people only discover they have the condition after suffering a heart attack or stroke.

For the elderly, the best approach is to measure blood pressure regularly. Although there are many simple home upper-arm blood pressure monitors on the market, it would be even more ideal to have a fitness device that can be worn all day and monitor automatically.

Apple Watch Blood Pressure Feature

With the launch of watchOS 26, five Apple Watch models can now measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models will not provide any readings — they will only send alerts when signs of possible high blood pressure are detected. Other devices similar to the Oura Ring also work in the same way.

Some fitness devices on the market can provide actual blood pressure readings, but they require periodic calibration using an upper-arm blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup Vital Signals says its Signal Ring smart ring does not require calibration, yet can match the accuracy of traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitors.

In an interview with Bloomberg, CEO Tom Moss revealed that he himself nearly died from undiagnosed high blood pressure — an experience that motivated him to found the company.

The Signal Ring will open for orders later today, with shipping in October, priced at US$399 and with no subscription required. The accompanying smartphone app can display real-time blood pressure readings and long-term trends (as shown in the image above).

It is worth noting that, although clinical trials have shown the Oura Ring can provide accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants, it has not yet received approval from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

Interestingly, Moss himself is not particularly keen on promoting the Signal Ring to all consumers. He believes this feature is best suited for the elderly and those assessed by doctors as being at risk of hypertension — comments that suggest the Signal Ring may not be particularly outstanding in other areas (such as sleep tracking).
